content: This product may contain inactive ingredients that could potentially trigger allergic reactions or other complications. Telavancin has the potential to induce a condition known as QT prolongation, which affects the heart's rhythm. The likelihood of QT prolongation increases if you have specific medical conditions or are taking other medications that also carry this risk. Additionally, low levels of potassium or magnesium in the blood can elevate the risk of QT prolongation. This risk may be further heightened if you are using certain drugs, such as diuretics (commonly referred to as water pills), or if you experience conditions like severe sweating, diarrhea, or vomiting. Telavancin may interfere with the efficacy of live bacterial vaccines, such as the typhoid vaccine. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when absolutely necessary, as it may harm an unborn baby. Consult your doctor for further details. It is currently unknown whether this medication passes into breast milk. Drug interactions can alter the effectiveness of your medications or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Maintain a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs as well as herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Telavancin may interfere with certain laboratory tests, such as coagulation tests (e.g., PT/INR/aPTT) or urine protein tests, potentially leading to inaccurate results. In the event of an overdose, if someone exhibits severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. While using this medication, laboratory and/or medical tests (e.g., kidney function tests) may be conducted. Ensure you attend all medical and laboratory appointments. It is crucial to adhere to the prescribed dosing schedule for this medication. If you miss a dose, consult your doctor or pharmacist promptly to establish a new dosing schedule. For storage instructions, refer to the product guidelines or consult your pharmacist. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. Properly dispose of this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not encompass all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for individualized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for comprehensive information about this product and your specific health needs. Telavancin is an antibiotic used to treat serious bacterial infections of the skin and certain types of pneumonia. It is administered via injection into a vein, typically once daily, as directed by your doctor. The injection should be given slowly over 60 minutes. If you are administering this medication at home, ensure you are thoroughly trained in its preparation and usage by a healthcare professional. Before use, visually inspect the product for particles or discoloration; do not use the liquid if either is present. Infusion reactions may occur if this drug is injected too quickly. Notify your doctor immediately if you experience symptoms of an infusion reaction, such as flushing of the upper body. For optimal effectiveness, use this antibiotic at evenly spaced intervals. Continue using the medication for the full prescribed duration, even if symptoms resolve after a few days. Common side effects may include a metallic or soapy taste, nausea, vomiting, or foamy urine. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Rarely, this medication may cause a severe intestinal condition due to a bacteria called Clostridioides difficile (C. difficile). This condition may occur during treatment or weeks to months after treatment has ceased. Prolonged or repeated use of this medication may result in oral thrush or a new vaginal yeast infection. Severe allergic reactions to this drug are rare. If you are in the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. Before using telavancin, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Adults with moderate to severe kidney disease who are using telavancin to treat serious lung infections may face an increased risk of death. Telavancin may cause or worsen kidney problems, particularly in individuals with heart failure, kidney disease, diabetes, or high blood pressure, or those taking certain medications. Kidney function tests must be performed before starting treatment, during treatment, and after completing treatment to monitor for kidney problems. Inform your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. Your doctor may order a pregnancy test before starting this medication. You should not become pregnant while using telavancin, as it may harm an unborn baby. Women of childbearing age should discuss reliable forms of birth control with their doctor while using this medication and for two days after the last dose.
